info.title: KuikCode API
info.description:
Create KuikCodes, change where a printed code points, read scans and manage folders and webhooks from your own systems.

## Authentication

Every request carries an API key from Settings, Developers: `Authorization: Bearer kc_live_...`. Keys belong to a workspace and are read-only or read and write. The API is included from the PRO plan.

## Conventions

- JSON in and out, UTF-8, ISO 8601 timestamps in UTC.
- Lists page with an opaque `cursor`; follow `next_cursor` until it is null.
- Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on POST to make retries safe for 24 hours; a replay answers with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.
- Rate limits are per key and per minute: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` come back on every response, `Retry-After` on a 429. Writes draw from a budget a third the size of reads.

## Errors

Every error is `{ "error": { "code", "message", "param"? } }` with the matching HTTP status.

| Status | `code` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | The body or query failed validation, or breaks a rule (unknown folder, a scan host you do not own). `param` names the field. |
| 401 | `invalid_api_key` | The Authorization header is missing, malformed, or the key was revoked. |
| 401 | `expired_api_key` | The key passed its expiry date. Create a new one in Settings, Developers. |
| 403 | `plan_required` | The workspace's plan does not include the API or this feature (webhooks, GPS, access codes). |
| 403 | `insufficient_scope` | A read-only key was used on a request that changes data. |
| 403 | `forbidden` | A plan ceiling was reached (codes, folders, pages, bulk rows) or the action is not allowed for this workspace. |
| 404 | `not_found` | No resource with that id in this workspace, or no endpoint at that path. |
| 409 | `conflict` | The change collides with existing data, for example a folder moved inside itself. |
| 409 | `preview_changed` | The rows behind a bulk `previewHash` changed since the preview. Run the preview again and confirm with the new hash. |
| 409 | `idempotency_in_progress` | A request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is still running. Retry in a moment to get its result. |
| 422 | `idempotency_mismatch` | The `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a different endpoint or payload. Use a new key. |
| 413 | `payload_too_large` | The request body is over the accepted size. |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | The per-minute budget for this key is spent. Wait for the seconds in `Retry-After`. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | Something failed on our side; the request is safe to retry. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | A dependency (the rate limiter) could not be reached for a write. Retry after `Retry-After`. |

## Versioning

The path carries the major version (`/v1`). Additive changes (new fields, new endpoints, new enum values) ship without notice; anything that would break a client gets a new major version and at least three months of overlap, announced in the changelog.

429.description: Rate limit reached. Retry after the seconds in Retry-After.

post.description: Creates a dynamic KuikCode. The destination is a URL, a KuikPage, or smart rules (PRO) that send scans to different places by device, country, language, time, date, weekday, scan count or location. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe.

400.description: Invalid body, or a logo that is not an image

403.description: The plan does not include a requested feature, or the code limit is reached.

patch.description: Repoint, refile, retag or archive up to 100 codes in one call. Ids from other workspaces are skipped silently.

post.description: Up to the plan's batch size per call (see `limits.bulkBatch` on GET /me), all into one folder, all or nothing. Send `csv` to import a file as the dashboard would; `dryRun: true` returns a preview with a `previewHash` to confirm with. Ten batches per ten minutes per key; dry runs are free.

200.description: The dry-run preview. Nothing was created.

400.description: Invalid rows, or a CSV with problems (the message lists the first ones)

409.description: A GTIN is already in use, or previewHash no longer matches

post.summary: Preview a restyle of a code
post.description: Renders the code with new colours, shape or tweaks applied, without saving anything. Then PATCH the same fields to make it real.

post.summary: Save a code's design as a template
post.description: Copies the code's design (not its destination) into a saved template the workspace can start new codes from, with the code's thumbnail as the preview. Counts against the plan's template ceiling.

get.description: One code with its destination, folder and tags. `scans` is only filled on the list; use GET /codes/{id}/scans or GET /analytics/summary for counts.

404.description: No such code in this workspace

patch.description: Rename, refile, retag, archive, or change where the code points. Fields left out stay as they are.

delete.description: Permanent. A printed copy of this code stops working. Archive instead if it may still be in the wild.

post.description: Reads a website's brand colours (its stylesheet and brand image) or takes a palette, and renders the batch's nine designed variants. Pick one and create the code with `design: { kind: "auto", url, batch, index }`. Pass `index` and `colors` to see one variant in your own colours before creating it. Twelve calls per minute per key.

400.description: No url or palette, or the site could not be read

403.description: The plan does not include Auto Design

post.description: Renders exactly what POST /codes would save for this `design` (a template with new colours, a plain code with a gold frame, an Auto Design variant with SCAN on top) without creating anything. Same render budget as /design/auto.

200.description: One 512 px PNG of the finished design.

400.description: Invalid design, or colours that would not scan

403.description: The plan does not include this design

get.description: The whole folder tree in one response, no paging. Group by `parentId` to rebuild it.

post.description: Creates a folder at the workspace root or inside `parentId`.

get.description: One folder.

patch.description: Rename, describe or move a folder. `parentId: null` moves it to the root; moving a folder inside itself is refused.

400.description: Cannot move a folder into itself

delete.description: Subfolders go with it. Codes inside are kept and move to the workspace root.

Queues the same payload again, with the same delivery id. Meant for deliveries that ended `failed`; a pending one is already scheduled.

patch.description: Change the receiving URL, pause or resume delivery, or replace the connected codes. `codeIds` replaces the whole set; codes left out are disconnected.

409.description: URL already used by another webhook

delete.description: The codes keep working; their scans simply stop being delivered.

post.description: Returns the webhook with its current signing secret. A POST rather than a GET so the reveal is an explicit action, never a side effect of listing.
Mints a new secret and returns it. For the next 24 hours every delivery carries two `v1` signatures, one per secret, so the receiver can switch without dropping events.

post.description: POSTs a signed sample `scan.created` (with `test: true`) to the URL and reports what the receiver answered.

get.description: Every KuikPage in the workspace, most recently changed first, with its live address when published.

200.description: Every KuikPage in the workspace, most recently changed first.

post.description: Creates a draft KuikPage from a template: `templateId` for a curated one or `orgTemplateId` for a saved one (see GET /page-templates). The address `{subdomain}.kuik.page` is claimed now and goes live on publish. Counts against the plan's KuikPages.

201.description: The new draft, with its content and preview link.

400.description: Unknown template or a name that breaks the rules

403.description: KuikPage limit reached, or the template uses blocks the plan does not include

get.description: One KuikPage with its status, live address and preview image.
KuikCode's curated templates and the workspace's saved ones. Every new KuikPage starts from one.

200.description: Curated first, then the workspace's, newest first.

get.description: Without `types`: every block type with its label and the plan it needs. With `types=buttons,map`: the JSON Schema of each named type, the fields an addBlock or setBlock operation may send. Fields with a default can be left out.

schema.description: Comma-separated block types.

parameters.description: Comma-separated block types.
parameters.name: types

200.description: Block types, with schemas when asked for.

get.description: The whole document: pages, their blocks with ids, theme and navigation, plus the revision to send with edits and signed preview links.

post.description: Applies a list of edit operations to the draft, in order, all or nothing. Operations: setBlock, addBlock, removeBlock, moveBlock (blocks by id), setTheme, setNav, addPage, removePage, setPage, movePage. The header at the top of a page stays first and cannot be removed; home stays first and has no address. `revision` must be the page's current one: if the page changed since you read it, the answer is 409 and you read it again.

200.description: The updated draft with its new revision.

400.description: An operation is invalid; the message names which one and why

403.description: The result needs a plan feature the workspace does not have

409.description: The page changed since that revision

post.description: Puts the current draft live at its address, exactly as the editor's Publish button does. Codes pointing at the page show the new version right away. The first publish also gives the page its own KuikCode: an existing code that opens the page, or a new one, which counts toward the plan's code limit (at the limit the page publishes without one).

200.description: The live address, the published version number, and the KuikCode this publish made, if any.

403.description: The page uses something the plan does not include

get.description: Every hosted site in the workspace, newest first, with its live address.

post.description: Deploys a ZIP to https://{subdomain}.kuik.page/. The ZIP needs an index.html at its root (a single top folder is flattened). Static files only: HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, images, fonts, audio, video and PDF; anything else, such as .php, is skipped and listed in `skipped`. Up to 300 files, 5 MB per file and 15 MB in total. Counts against the plan's hosted site slots.

400.description: Not a ZIP, no index.html, too large, or a name that breaks the rules

get.description: One hosted site with its address, deploy number and size.

post.description: For ZIPs over about 3 MB. Returns a presigned URL: PUT the ZIP bytes there with `Content-Type: application/zip` and the exact `Content-Length` you declared, within 10 minutes, then pass `uploadId` to POST /sites or POST /sites/{id}/deploy. Each upload deploys once; one that is never deployed is deleted after a day.

Replaces every file of the site with a new ZIP, same rules as publishing. The address stays the same, so codes pointing at it keep working. Visitors switch to the new version only once every file is in place.

400.description: Not a ZIP, no index.html or too large

get.description: The finished design as an image: frame, stickers, logo and all, exactly what the dashboard downloads. PNG and JPG at the requested pixel size, SVG as vectors with the frame embedded as a raster. Mesh shader frames render as a gradient. Add `response=url` to get a public download link instead of the bytes.

schema.description: Edge length in pixels for png and jpg; the drawing resolution for svg.

parameters.description: Edge length in pixels for png and jpg; the drawing resolution for svg.
parameters.name: size

schema.description: Hex colour behind the code for jpg (no alpha channel). Default white.

parameters.description: Hex colour behind the code for jpg (no alpha channel). Default white.

post.description: Creates a picture from a text description and stores it in the workspace Library as a JPEG. Takes a few seconds. Each call counts toward the plan's monthly AI generated images, including prompts the safety filter blocks.

400.description: Prompt blocked by the safety filter, or invalid

403.description: Not included in the plan, the month's allowance is used up, or the Library is full

post.description: Stores an image in the workspace Library, from a public https URL or as base64, and returns its CDN URL for KuikPage blocks. PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG; raster images are re-encoded to WebP and capped at 2400 px on the long edge.

201.description: The stored image. width and height are null for SVG.

400.description: Not a public URL, not an image, or an unsupported type

get.description: Free Pexels photos (commercial use, no attribution needed). An empty query returns a curated selection. Import one with POST /stock/photos/{id}/import before using it on a page.

post.description: Copies a Pexels photo into the workspace Library at up to 1280 px wide and returns its CDN URL.

apiKey.description: An API key from Settings, Developers: `Authorization: Bearer kc_live_...`

sites.description: Hosted sites on kuik.page. 0 means not included; null means unlimited.

aiImages.description: Generated images per month (POST /images/generate). 0 means not included.

bulkBatch.description: Rows per bulk create call. 0 means bulk create is not included.

apiRequestsPerMinute.description: Read budget per key; writes get a third.

autoDesign.description: design.kind = auto on POST /codes and POST /design/auto.

features.description: What this workspace's plan lets the API do; a false here explains a plan_required error before it happens.

apiKeys.description: Live API keys in the workspace.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code, see the table in the introduction.

param.description: The request field the error is about, when there is one.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page; null on the last page.

shortCode.description: The 9 character id printed in the scan link. Never changes.

scanUrl.description: The link encoded in the artwork.

archived.description: Archived codes stop redirecting and serve a 'no longer active' page.

previewUrl.description: 300 px thumbnail of the artwork, when the dashboard has rendered one.

scans.description: Lifetime scans. Present on list responses.

type.description: `url`, `page` or `smartRules` for codes made through the API; codes designed in the dashboard may carry other kinds (vcard, event, wifi, map, geolocation, gs1DigitalLink...).

url.description: Where a scan lands, when the kind has one address. For smart rules, the fallback.

fallbackUrl.description: Smart rules: where scans land when no rule matches.

rules.description: Smart rules in evaluation order; null for other kinds.

summary.description: The one-line description the dashboard shows.

joins.description: How condition i connects to condition i+1, evaluated left to right. Omit for all `and`.

value.description: Local time of the scanner's timezone.

valueEnd.description: End of the window for `between`; a window past midnight wraps.

value.description: Scans of this code so far.

warnings.description: Human sentences about compromises made, for the caller to relay.

archetype.description: Auto Design family that was applied (clean, branded, framedText...).

palette.description: Colours the design was built from, lead first.

scanVerified.description: true when the rendered design decoded in our scanner check.

folderId.description: Folder to file the code in; omit or null for the workspace root.

scanHost.description: Print the code on your branded scan host (your kuikco.de subdomain or an active custom domain) instead of the shared kuikco.de/p/ link. Fixed once the code exists.

gps.description: Ask scanners for their precise location (PRO). Off by default.

webhookUrl.description: https endpoint that receives every scan (Business).

accessCode.description: Password visitors type before the destination opens (PRO). Never readable again.

pageId.description: A KuikPage in this workspace. The code follows the page's address.

fallbackUrl.description: Where scans land when no rule matches.

rules.description: Checked in order; the first match wins.

url.description: Website to take the brand colours from. Defaults to the destination when that is a URL.

palette.description: Skip discovery and design from these hex colours, lead colour first.

batch.description: Each batch is a different deck of variants for the same colours. Increase to see new options.

index.description: Which variant of the batch to apply, from POST /design/auto. Omit for the first.

colors.description: Recolor the finished design: its distinct colours, code first and frame last, are replaced one for one by these. The first colour becomes the ink; it must still read against the design's background (2.5:1 at least, 4.5:1 for a warning-free result) or the request is refused with the ratio.

shape.description: Outline of the code and its frame. Omit to keep the design's own; `circle` for a round one, `square` for a squared frame, `decagon`, `dodecagon`, `hexadecagon` or `icosagon` for a ten, twelve, sixteen or twenty sided one.

colors.description: Recolor the finished design: its distinct colours, code first and frame last, are replaced one for one by these. The first colour becomes the ink; it must still read against the design's background (2.5:1 at least, 4.5:1 for a warning-free result) or the request is refused with the ratio.

shape.description: Outline of the code and its frame. Omit to keep the design's own; `circle` for a round one, `square` for a squared frame, `decagon`, `dodecagon`, `hexadecagon` or `icosagon` for a ten, twelve, sixteen or twenty sided one.

oneOf.description: The workspace Brand Kit: its colours, its logo in the centre.

colors.description: Recolor the finished design: its distinct colours, code first and frame last, are replaced one for one by these. The first colour becomes the ink; it must still read against the design's background (2.5:1 at least, 4.5:1 for a warning-free result) or the request is refused with the ratio.

shape.description: Outline of the code and its frame. Omit to keep the design's own; `circle` for a round one, `square` for a squared frame, `decagon`, `dodecagon`, `hexadecagon` or `icosagon` for a ten, twelve, sixteen or twenty sided one.

oneOf.description: Black on white, no frame; `colors`, `shape` and `tweaks` adjust it.

DesignInput.description: How the code looks. Omit for plain black on white; assistants creating a code for a website should send { kind: "auto" }.

thickness.description: Band width, 0 hairline to 100 chunky; the editor's slider. 50 is the default.

style.description: Square codes: `band` runs the frame the same width all the way round; `label` sets the bottom text large in a band of its own under the code.

color.description: Solid frame colour. Without a colour, gradient, split or shader, a new design's frame takes the dots' colours.

gradient.description: Frame as a gradient of these colours.

split.description: Frame in two colours, split vertically, horizontally or as a pie.

shader.description: Animated-looking mesh or silk texture on the band, in these colours.

ring.description: An extra ring wrapped outside the frame.

glow.description: Glow on the frame's rings, words and shapes: `soft` (or true) for a halo in their own colour, `neon` for white-hot lines lit in their colour, `off` (or false) for none.

overlay.description: What repeats around the band: nothing, a repeated word, a repeated shape, or one or two rings.

ringStyle.description: How the one or two rings are drawn, in the border styles but `tapered`: `solid`, `dotted`, `double`, `outlined`, `sketch` (three loose pencil passes), `ribbon` (a twisting ribbon), `wave` (a thick and thin line over lighter crescents) or `swell` (the wave, its crests rising).

repeatedText.description: The word repeated around the band (sets overlay to text).

repeatedShape.description: The motif repeated around the band (sets overlay to shape).

topText.description: Word at the top of the frame, like SCAN. Empty string removes it.

bottomText.description: Word at the bottom, like TAP ON SCREEN. Empty string removes it.

overlayColor.description: Colour of the words and motifs on the band.

toEdge.description: Dots to the edge: the dots around a round or polygon code run out to the outer border (or to the edge without one) and are cut cleanly there. No effect on square codes or with the inner border on.

look.description: A finished eye in one go, the editor's Looks: `square`, `rounded`, `circle`, `dot` (square frame, round center), `diamond`, `drop` (round, the corner facing the code sharp), `petal` (round, the outer corner sharp) or `leaf` (both sharp). Applied first; the fields below fine-tune it.

roundness.description: Fine control instead of shape: 0 square, 25 rounded, 50 circle.

followFrame.description: The center takes the frame's shape, sharp corners included, instead of innerShape.

sharpInteriorCorners.description: Each eye's corner facing the code stays crisp.

sharpExteriorCorners.description: Each eye's corner pointing away from the code stays crisp.

style.description: The borders' style: `sketch` draws three loose pencil passes, `ribbon` twists as it runs, `wave` is a thick-and-thin line with a pale band and brighter crescents, `swell` is that wave with its outside edge rising at every crest. The inner border always takes it; the outer border with `applyToOuter`.

applyToOuter.description: The outer border takes the style too. Ignored on a styled edge (the outer border follows the edge) and for `tapered`, which needs line ends. When only the outer border shows, a style alone turns this on.

thickness.description: 0 thin to 100 thick; the editor's slider.

glow.description: Glow on both borders: `soft` (or true), `neon` or `off` (or false).

edge.description: Edge treatment of the code's outline: `swell` is eight slow swells round the rim, `ribbon` the leaning, rounded teeth of a twisted ribbon's outline.

url.description: Public https URL of the logo image.

data.description: Base64 of the image bytes (no data: prefix), up to 5 MB decoded.

LogoInput.description: A logo for the centre of the code: PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG up to 5 MB, by URL or as base64. Stored in the workspace Library.

Utm.description: Campaign parameters appended to the destination on every scan.

failed.description: Codes that could not be changed and why. Folder and archive changes apply to every id at once; destination and tag changes apply code by code, so a failure here leaves the others done.

allOf.description: Point every listed code at the same place.
Point a printed code somewhere new. The artwork never changes.

accessCode.description: A value sets or replaces the access code, null removes it.

url.description: Public https URL of the logo image.

data.description: Base64 of the image bytes (no data: prefix), up to 5 MB decoded.

logo.description: A logo sets or replaces the centre logo, null removes it. The artwork is re-rendered.
